reasoning: This is accepted work: the person's own instruction two days ago, admitted with its own checkpoint, and the rewrite is built and verified. The document is explicit that his eye is not the gate: "A shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery. Once the verifier confirms the observable outcome, the pipeline shows the result — the changed document, the passing check, the running page, whatever the decision sheet named — and closes the checkpoint in the same step. It never leaves a row open to wait for the human to look at what was already shown and bless it." The three cases reserved for him are "a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a change to the definition of correct that is still an open fork — never an ordinary buildable result a command, a test, or a plain read already confirms was delivered." Wording could look like a taste call, but he settled that fork himself when he ordered plain language: "A redefinition he ordered himself is not that third case: he settled the fork when he ordered it, and carrying out his decision is executing it, not making it." Nor does the change reach past what he ordered — eleven titles rewritten is exactly the instruction, so the converse clause about behaviour "he never named" does not bite. The outcome is confirmed without him: plan_checks.py exits 0 naming each rewritten row, and the regenerated board page is the rendered surface ("Where the DOD names a rendered or published surface — the words page, board.html, link, published, rendered, url — a receipt with no --surface is refused"), so verify carries the board page as its surface. Nothing here is irreversible outside git, so rule 12's stop-for-his-word ground is untouched. That he is asleep is irrelevant: the pipeline "continue[s] without waiting for the person's attention," and if he dislikes a title later, "that disagreement is a new fact, not a reopening of the one that shipped."
